facts.fact: Government decree no. 2020-777 of 5 October 2020 sets the conditions and procedures for electronic data exchange between structures (public bodies and bodies running a public service) and between them and their users, applying decree-law of the Head of Government no. 2020-31 of 10 June 2020; it enters into force on 1 January 2021 (art. 28) and was published in JORT no. 100.
facts.system: Decree-law no. 2020-31 and government decree no. 2020-777 on electronic data exchange

facts.fact: Government decree no. 2020-777 of 5 October 2020 says public structures must use electronic exchange among themselves and with users (art. 4), must make the list of their available data flows and licences available to the interoperability operator (art. 20), and may not demand more than one electronic copy of a document (art. 11); the text is binding from 1 January 2021.
facts.system: Decree-law no. 2020-31 and government decree no. 2020-777 on electronic data exchange

facts.fact: Government decree no. 2020-777 of 5 October 2020 is itself the implementing decree made under decree-law no. 2020-31, creating the interoperability operator's duties (art. 18) and a Strategic Committee and a Coordination Committee (arts. 21-25); the document is dated 2020 and gives no later application.
facts.system: Decree-law no. 2020-31 and government decree no. 2020-777 on electronic data exchange

systems.owner: interoperability operator (personne publique), under the ministry in charge of communication technologies
systems.tiers: structures publiques and other structures running a public service

facts.fact: Circular of the Head of Government no. 04 of 2026 lists among its references decree-law no. 31 of 10 June 2020 on electronic data exchange between structures and their users and between structures, as approved by law no. 14 of 7 April 2021; the date of the fact is the approving law, and the circular is of 28 August 2026.
facts.system: Decree-law no. 2020-31 on electronic data exchange, approved by law no. 14 of 2021

note: Loi n 2026-16 of 20 July 2026 is a one-article act approving the 2026-2030 development plan; it says nothing of public bodies sharing data.
Companion page to the 2026-2030 development plan; the passages held cover digitalisation, AI and data centres generally and state nothing on a law or decree on public bodies sharing data.
Procurement notice of 2026-09-03 for consultants to draft a health-sector interoperability framework; a plan with nothing contracted, delivered or adopted, and no statement on this study.

facts.fact: Tunisia's Presidency of the Government says Decree-law 31 of 2020 (10 June 2020) on electronic exchange of data between public structures and with their users is in force, with its conditions and procedures set by Government order 777 of 5 October 2020.
The Presidency says the decree-law establishes the principle that users are not asked for data or documents public bodies already hold or that are available through the interconnection platform.

note: The deck mentions a new legal framework without naming a data sharing law or decree.

facts.fact: The ministry's FAQ lists Government Order No. 777 of 5 October 2020 on the conditions and procedures for applying Decree-Law No. 31 of 2020 on electronic exchange of data between public bodies and their dealers and among bodies.
